spec-driven-development: Writes a spec with goals, scope and acceptance criteria before coding
brainstorming: Asks one question at a time to pin down requirements, then writes a design doc
grilling: Questions a plan or decision relentlessly to expose gaps (30 lines, lightweight)
create-prd: Writes a lean 8-section PRD: background, goals, segments, value proposition, solution, release
to-tickets: Splits a plan or conversation into thin tickets with dependencies and files them in your tracker
writing-plans: Turns a spec into an implementation plan of small file- and test-level steps
planning-with-files: Keeps task_plan, findings and progress.md on disk and re-injects them via hooks to resume long work
api-and-interface-design: Applies criteria for stable REST/GraphQL APIs, module boundaries and type contracts
domain-modeling: Records domain terms in GLOSSARY.md and decisions as ADRs
improve-codebase-architecture: Finds chances to deepen modules, shows them in an HTML report, and debates each one
frontend-design: Steers Claude to a distinctive visual direction and typography, not a template look (Anthropic)
impeccable: Provides design commands (polish, bolder, critique, audit) to refine and review UI
taste-skill: Avoids AI-looking pages using art direction from 247 award sites, fixing via a screenshot loop
ui-ux-pro-max: Searches a database of styles, palettes and fonts to recommend a design system
web-design-guidelines: Checks UI code for accessibility and UX against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines (39 lines)
frontend-ui-engineering: Builds production-grade UI with accessibility (WCAG), responsiveness and state handling
incremental-implementation: Splits multi-file changes into thin verifiable slices and lands them one by one
subagent-driven-development: Hands each plan task to a fresh subagent with reviews between tasks
ponytail: Makes the smallest change that solves the task and keeps replies short, like a lazy senior dev
react-best-practices: Applies Vercel's React/Next.js performance rules for waterfalls, bundle size and re-renders
swiftui-pro: Reviews SwiftUI code for modern APIs, maintainability and performance (Paul Hudson)
ios-simulator: Builds, launches and drives iOS apps in the Simulator with 30 token-saving scripts
expo-router: Explains Expo Router file-based routing, tabs, modals and headers (official Expo)
react-native-best-practices: Applies Callstack's React Native performance guidance: FPS, TTI, bundle, leaks, FlashList
supabase-postgres: Gives Supabase's official Postgres rules to read before touching tables, indexes or RLS
modern-python: Sets up Python projects with uv, ruff and ty and migrates from pip, poetry and black
mcp-builder: Designs, builds and evaluates MCP servers in TypeScript or Python that wrap external APIs
test-driven-development: Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: watch a test fail before writing the implementation
tdd-lite: Gives short TDD guidance favoring integration tests (38 lines, low token cost)
webapp-testing: Runs a local web app with Playwright to check features, screenshots and console logs
browser-testing-devtools: Checks DOM, console, network and performance in a real browser via Chrome DevTools MCP
property-based-testing: Writes property-based tests with Hypothesis, fast-check or proptest to cover whole input spaces
systematic-debugging: Follows four debugging phases (investigate, hypothesize, verify, then fix) before changing code
diagnosing-bugs: Builds a reproduction loop first, then narrows down hard bugs and performance regressions
verification-before-completion: Runs verification commands and checks the output before claiming work is done
code-review-and-quality: Reviews code before merge on five axes: correctness, readability, design, security, performance
receiving-code-review: Verifies review feedback technically before applying it instead of following it blindly
find-bugs: Finds bugs, vulnerabilities and quality issues in the current branch's changes (75 lines)
second-opinion: Sends a diff to another model such as Codex or Gemini for an independent review
code-simplification: Simplifies hard-to-read code while keeping its behavior unchanged
security-and-hardening: Hardens input handling, auth, storage and integrations against OWASP risks
security-audit: Runs Cloudflare's multi-stage audit: map attack surface, form hypotheses, report only verified findings
sentry-security-review: Reviews code for evidence-backed vulnerabilities such as injection, XSS, authn and authz flaws
differential-review: Reviews changes for security using git blame, caller counts (blast radius) and test coverage
semgrep-scan: Detects languages, picks Semgrep rulesets, scans after approval and merges results as SARIF
supply-chain-risk-auditor: Audits dependencies for known advisories, abandoned upstreams and risky install scripts
gha-security-review: Finds exploitable paths in GitHub Actions workflows, such as pull_request_target and injection
agentic-actions-auditor: Audits CI-hosted AI agents (Claude Code Action, Codex) for paths reachable by attacker input
documentation-and-adrs: Records design decisions as ADRs and public API changes as docs to preserve context
doc-coauthoring: Co-writes specs, proposals and decision docs through context gathering, drafting and review
humanizer: Rewrites AI-sounding text using Wikipedia's AI-writing signs (English-focused)
git-workflow-and-versioning: Sets rules for atomic commits, branches, conflict resolution, splitting messy trees and PRs
using-git-worktrees: Creates an isolated git worktree before feature work to separate it from the current workspace
finishing-a-development-branch: After tests pass, picks merge, PR, keep or discard, and cleans up the worktree
pr-writer: Writes or refreshes PR titles and descriptions that are easy for reviewers to read
iterate-pr: Revises a PR repeatedly until CI is green and important review comments are resolved
handoff: Compacts the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent (16 lines)
ci-cd-and-automation: Sets up CI quality gates, test runners and deployment strategies
shipping-and-launch: Provides pre-launch checklists, monitoring, staged rollout and rollback plans
setup-pre-commit: Sets up Husky and lint-staged to run formatting, type checks and tests on commit
deploy-to-vercel: Deploys to Vercel as preview or production and returns the link
eas-app-stores: Builds iOS/Android with EAS and submits to TestFlight, App Store or Google Play, incl. signing and versions
performance-optimization: Measures first, then optimizes using Core Web Vitals, N+1 queries, bundle size and query evidence
observability-and-instrumentation: Adds logs, metrics, traces and alerts so production behavior can be diagnosed
docx: Creates and edits Word (.docx) files, tracked changes and templates
pdf: Extracts PDF text and tables, merges and splits files, fills forms, runs OCR
xlsx: Reads Excel and CSV files, handles formulas, formatting and charts, and verifies recalculation
pptx: Creates and edits PowerPoint files, templates and speaker notes
skill-creator: Creates skills and refines them with evals, benchmarks and trigger-description tuning (official)
writing-for-agents: Explains how to write skills, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md so agents follow them
claude-md-improver: Finds CLAUDE.md files in a repo, scores their quality and fixes them
claude-automation-recommender: Analyzes a codebase and recommends hooks, subagents, skills and MCP servers
claude-settings-audit: Detects the tech stack and builds a settings.json allowlist of mostly read-only commands
skill-scanner: Scans a skill before install for prompt injection, risky scripts and data exfiltration
hookify-writing-rules: Creates warn or block hooks for forbidden patterns from markdown rule files (hookify)
dispatching-parallel-agents: Splits 2+ independent tasks with no shared state across subagents to run in parallel
context-optimization: Cuts context budget and token cost via observation masking, cache-friendly prefixes and partitioning
caveman: Answers in an ultra-terse style that keeps technical content to save output tokens
session-report: Builds an HTML report of tokens, cache and costly prompts from ~/.claude/projects transcripts
careful: Warns before destructive Bash/PowerShell commands (rm -rf, DROP, force push) via a built-in hook
git-guardrails: Installs a PreToolUse hook that blocks push, reset --hard, clean and branch -D
